problems.title: Ex 1.1-1.4: magic numbers, address-space segments, von Neumann machines, segfaults
problems.anchor_text: Ex. 1.1 (5pts) | What is the role of the magic number for binary executable files?
subparts: 1.1 role of the magic number for binary executables; where stored
1.2 list all segments of an address space and explain each
1.3 what are von-Neumann machines; relation to today's computers
1.4 meaning of 'segmentation fault (core dumped)', causes, meaning of 'segmentation' and of 'core'
problems.grouped_with_reason: Four independent 5-pt textbook short-answer questions. specs.md states a few sentences each is sufficient, so they are far too small to justify one worker apiece; they share no constructed object, so grouping cannot make them inconsistent.

problems.title: Ex 1.5-1.8: compiler load-address assumptions, program launch path, contiguous-allocation address translation, round-robin
problems.anchor_text: Ex. 1.5 (5pts) | When a compiler generates the binary code for a source program
subparts: 1.5 why the compiler cannot know the load address; what assumptions it makes about where and how
1.6 all OS steps from double-click / typed command until the application appears on screen
1.7 finding the physical address from a virtual address under contiguous memory allocation
problems.grouped_with_reason: Same reasoning as p1: four independent 5-pt short-answer questions. Split 4+4 from p1 rather than 8-in-one so that neither worker's attention is spread across eight prompts.

problems.title: Ex 1.9: read, summarize and critically judge three papers FROM the 'OS History and Architecture' list
problems.anchor_text: Ex. 1.9 (30pts) | Pick three papers from 'OS History and Architecture' in the paper list.
subparts: pick three papers from rows 1-1..1-11 of PaperList
critically judge each (>= 1/3 page total per paper)
problems.grouped_with_reason: The three papers are one deliverable with a shared format and a shared no-overlap constraint; splitting per-paper would produce three fragments with inconsistent depth and citation style.

problems.title: Ex 1.0: search for, read, summarize and critically judge three OS History and Architecture papers NOT on the list
problems.anchor_text: Ex. 1.0 (30pts) | Search for three papers on the topic of 'OS History and Architecture'.
subparts: search out three papers on OS History and Architecture, none of them on the supplied list and none used in Ex 1.9
critically judge each (>= 1/3 page total per paper)
problems.grouped_with_reason: Kept separate from p3 and deliberately sequenced AFTER it: p4's brief names the three papers p3 actually used, plus all eleven list papers, as forbidden. Merging p3 and p4 into one worker would be 60 pts and six papers for one agent; running them in either order without the exclusion list is how the two answers end up overlapping.
